feedback.worked_solution:
We take the constant factor out of the integral and then apply the power rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =2\int {x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot (\frac{{x}^{(-2+1)}}{-2+1})+C \\  & =2\cdot (\frac{{x}^{-1}}{-1})+C \\  & =-2\cdot {x}^{-1}+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{x}+C\end{aligned}
$$
